Where the design stands

  • 108 design entries and 52 pinned declarations.
  • 5 open questions and 2 blocking questions.
  • 21 members with an implementation binding.

  • 42 outside Specs the Pack rests on; 69 outside Specs rest on the Pack; 31 outside Specs verify it; no outside Specs supersede it.

Mermaid source

Preferred syntax: block. Fixed categorical cells; membership appears in comments.

Framing

The design-management arc, in review order: the Pack page and the reader assembly it renders; entry locations, recipe parameters and shipped recipe files; the recipes used in design work; the engine build identity and the authoring watch loop. The remaining Specs capture promises of the original design across the model, consumers, validation and observation. Pack design shows each member's stated next rung, design columns and code bindings.

1. The Design Review's Pack page presents the Pack's design

spec:decisions.pack-design-page

The Design Review's Pack page presents the Pack's design

spec:decisions.pack-design-pageDecision Record · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/decisions/pack-design-page.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Let a person working in the repository read where a Pack's design stands, what holds each member below its stated next rung, what the Pack rests on, and which code answers to it, on the page the Protocol already generates.
Decision
context
The Design Review's Pack page lists the members with their readiness and bindings, and the verifier gaps. The first adopter designs whole capabilities ahead of their code as Packs and generates its own page beside the Design Review, walking the readiness floor one rung above the stated rung, reading what the members rest on outside the Pack, joining the open questions, and re-parsing carrier files for entry lines. Its design passes read that page first. The shipped projections are frozen, so the Pack page cannot change until a decision narrows the freeze for it.
decision
The Design Review's Pack page renders the Pack design that spec:consumers.pack-design assembles: a member table in authored order with each member's stated rung, floor reached, the rung above the stated rung with the clause that holds it there, its design columns and its bindings; a section naming what holds each member below its stated next rung; the Specs outside the Pack that members rest on and that rest on members; each member's open questions with their entry addresses and source lines; and each member's realizing and referencing code units with their roles and their components' layers and contexts. The verifier gaps and findings stay. The freeze on the four shipped projections stands for everything else, the Spec page and the index included.
rationale
  • The assembly already exists as graph data and reader values, and an adopter that rebuilds it by hand evaluates the floor a second way, which can disagree with the reader's. One assembly in the reader, rendered on the page the Protocol ships, gives a reviewer the design as it stands and leaves the adopter's script nothing to recompute.
alternatives
  • Starting the Spec Studio with an HTML Pack page is closer to the original design, but the Studio is a later arc, and the Pack design data serves it unchanged.
  • Shipping the assembly as data only keeps every projection frozen and leaves rendering to each adopter, which is the burden this record removes.
consequences
  • Line links on the page point into carrier files through the graph's location table, so the page stays a function of the graph alone.

2. The Pack context carries the Pack's design

spec:consumers.pack-design

The Pack context carries the Pack's design

spec:consumers.pack-designUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A capability designed ahead of its code is read as a Pack: its members in reading order, how far each has matured, what design each carries, what it rests on, and which code answers to it. The reader holds every one of those facts. This Spec assembles them once on the Pack context so a page, a recipe and an adopter's script read one answer.

Intent
problem
Reading a Pack's design means joining member readiness, the floor one rung above the stated rung, design entries, decisions, open questions, code bindings with their components, and the Specs outside the Pack, and every consumer that joins them by hand reads the floor or the boundary a different way.
outcome
Give each Pack member its design columns and give the Pack its boundary on the Pack context, so the Design Review, a recipe and an adopter's page read the design from one assembly.
Behavior
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md:28
One helper derives a Spec's design columns; the Spec context carries them as designColumns and each resolved Pack member carries the same value as design, while the Pack context carries the boundary.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md:29
A member's stated next rung is the rung above its stated rung, none when it states ready. Its unmet clauses come from the one floor evaluator with that rung as the target, each failure with its targets when it has them. The list is empty when the floor already holds the stated next rung, so the rung waits for its author's statement, never a promotion. The floor reached and the failures at the rung above it are separate readings.
rule line 30 · specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md:30
A member's design columns count its keyed design and ui entries other than description, its pinned declarations under the contract-declarations rule, and its open questions with how many block. They list each question with its zero-based authored index, text, blocking flag, optional key, decider, links, provisional and trigger as present, and optional source line from the location table. They list the decisions it names through decidedBy, each with its stated rung or unresolved when the target is no Spec. The columns are counts and lists read from the graph, never a score or a rung.
rule line 31 · specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md:31
A member lists the code units that satisfy it and those that reference it as code unit bindings; each binding carries codeId and claim, plus label, file, line and role when recorded. A component unit carries its own optional layer and context; a memberOf edge adds its component's id and optional layer and context. The Spec context carries the same bindings.
rule line 32 · specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md:32
A member counts its verifiers and enabled verifiers, and the example Specs that declare verifies on it with how many are enabled, using the reader's verifier decoding.
rule line 33 · specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md:33
The Pack's boundary lists the Specs outside the Pack joined to a member by an authored relation. A Spec a member relates to by refines, dependsOn, constrainedBy or decidedBy is one the Pack rests on; a Spec that relates to a member by the same four relations is one that rests on the Pack. The boundary lists inbound verifies separately as verifiedBy and inbound supersedes as supersededBy, with the same row shape. Each row carries the outside Spec's id, title, stated rung and whether it carries implemented, and for each relation type the members it joins, the types in the closed relation list's order and the members in authored order. A relation whose target is not a Spec in the graph is left to referential integrity and does not appear.
rule line 34 · specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md:34
Members keep the manifest's authored order, unresolved members carry their unresolved row without design columns, and boundary rows sort by id in code-unit order.
rule line 35 · specs/consumers/pack-design.sdp.md:35
The assembly is a pure function of the graph: it reads no carrier file, records nothing, and confers no delivery fact or readiness.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.architectural-annotation

    Architectural significance is annotated on the anchor of the unit that realizes it. A code anchor may carry role, the architectural pattern the unit plays; a component: anchor may additionally carry layer, one of edge, application, domain, adapter, or infrastructure, and context, its bounded context. The component: anchor is anchored architecture: it is the declared component, and there is no separate architecture file, because the anchor sits where the component is realized. It is not the original design's declared Component that could exist before code; an unrealized component lives in Specs and never as an invented CodeNode. A role is a free, corpus-owned vocabulary whose taxonomy the census renders with counts from the graph; service, decider, projection, read-model, codec, contract, barrel, and utility are the lineage set, not a closed list. layer is a closed set, and a value outside it is an envelope error; layer or context on a non-component anchor is an envelope error. All three attributes are optional, and omission is lawful.

A Pack page shows where the Pack's design stands

specs/consumers/design-review.pack-design-page.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Render a Pack's design assembly as one deterministic Markdown page a reviewer reads before a design pass, between iterations and before stating readiness.
Behavior
rule line 21 · specs/consumers/design-review.pack-design-page.sdp.md:21
The page keeps its title line, framing and vocabulary references, then renders, in this order: the member table, what holds each member below its stated next rung, the Pack's boundary, the open questions, the code, the verifier coverage gaps, and the findings.
rule line 22 · specs/consumers/design-review.pack-design-page.sdp.md:22
The member table has one row per member in authored order: the linked Spec with its position from 1 and its title, kind, altitude, stated rung, floor reached, the stated next rung with nothing blocks when its unmet clauses are empty and the first unmet clause otherwise, the design columns as counts (entries, declarations, questions with the blocking count), the decisions it names, and the implementation and verifier binding columns with the present and none values spec:consumers.binding-language-views fixes for every aggregate table, beside a design-reference column that reads present when a code unit references the member and none otherwise. Unit counts stay off the table, which offers existence and never a degree. An unresolved member keeps a row that says so, and the later sections skip it, because the graph holds none of its data.
rule line 23 · specs/consumers/design-review.pack-design-page.sdp.md:23
The section for the stated next rung lists each member with unmet clauses at its stated next rung, every clause with the targets it names and their stated rungs. A member whose floor already holds its stated next rung is listed apart as waiting for its author's statement, which the page never presents as approval.
rule line 24 · specs/consumers/design-review.pack-design-page.sdp.md:24
The boundary section lists, in order, Rests on, Rested on by, Verified by and Superseded by, from restsOn, restedOnBy, verifiedBy and supersededBy. Each empty list reads None.; otherwise a table gives each row with the linked Spec, its stated rung, its implementation binding, present or none, and the members it joins under each relation type.
rule line 25 · specs/consumers/design-review.pack-design-page.sdp.md:25
The open-questions section groups questions by member in authored order. Each question shows its blocking flag, its entry address when it carries a key, its text, and a link to its line in the carrier file when the location table records one.
rule line 26 · specs/consumers/design-review.pack-design-page.sdp.md:26
The code section lists, per member, each realizing and each referencing unit with its id, a link to its file and line, its role, and its component with that component's layer and context, under the binding-language headings the Design Review already uses. A member with no unit says so in one line.
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/design-review.pack-design-page.sdp.md:27
A line link is a relative link from the page to the carrier or source file with a #L<line> fragment, encoded as spec:consumers.design-review states.

Decisions

  • The Design Review's Pack page presents the Pack's design

    The Design Review's Pack page renders the Pack design that spec:consumers.pack-design assembles: a member table in authored order with each member's stated rung, floor reached, the rung above the stated rung with the clause that holds it there, its design columns and its bindings; a section naming what holds each member below its stated next rung; the Specs outside the Pack that members rest on and that rest on members; each member's open questions with their entry addresses and source lines; and each member's realizing and referencing code units with their roles and their components' layers and contexts. The verifier gaps and findings stay. The freeze on the four shipped projections stands for everything else, the Spec page and the index included.

4. The graph records where each addressable entry is written

spec:extraction.entry-locations

The graph records where each addressable entry is written

spec:extraction.entry-locationsUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/extraction/entry-locations.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

An entry address names one keyed Design or UI entry, one keyed rule or flow, one keyed open question, or one keyed Model term. A reader following an address needs its recorded source line.

Intent
problem
The graph records the file of a Spec and the line of every anchor, but not the line of an entry inside a Spec, so a page that links an address to its text, or a review that cites one, re-reads carrier syntax the extractor already parsed.
outcome
Record source lines for Design and UI entries, rules and flows, Model terms, open questions and their optional fields, and authored relation targets beside the graph's nodes, so consumers locate text without parsing carriers.
Behavior
rule line 20 · specs/extraction/entry-locations.sdp.md:20
The graph carries a location table beside its nodes and edges. Each row names a Spec id, carrier file, entry and 1-based source line. Entries are design.<key> or ui.<key> for keys other than description, rule[<i>] or flow[<i>] for entries of the primary behavior owner, term[<i>] for a Model term, question[<i>] for an open question, question[<i>].decider, question[<i>].links, question[<i>].provisional or question[<i>].trigger for each of those optional fields present, and relation.<type>.<target> for an authored relation target. Indexes count from 0 within their authored lists, a term's among the Spec's terms in authored order. A rule, flow, term or question row carries key when that entry has one.
rule line 21 · specs/extraction/entry-locations.sdp.md:21
Primitive and Pack nodes stay free of lines, so a comparison of nodes and edges is unchanged by an edit that only moves an entry, and carrier parity compares nodes and edges and never the location table, whose lines differ by carrier by nature.
rule line 22 · specs/extraction/entry-locations.sdp.md:22
Markdown and TypeScript record the entry forms their syntax carries. TypeScript questions are located at the question property or string literal. Gherkin records its Rule lines and authored or defaulted relation sites; it carries no Design, UI or Model section, open question or question field. A missing row means not located, never absent.
rule line 23 · specs/extraction/entry-locations.sdp.md:23
An authored relation target has a location row whose entry is relation.<type>.<target>, at its carrier's recorded relation site. A defaulted Gherkin relation uses the Scenario identity line when no explicit relation tag locates it.
rule line 24 · specs/extraction/entry-locations.sdp.md:24
Rows sort by Spec id, then by entry, in code-unit order. The table is a deterministic function of the carriers at the extracted commit, as every other part of the graph is.
rule line 25 · specs/extraction/entry-locations.sdp.md:25
A location names where an entry is written and nothing else: it is not an identity, never an anchor target or a binding, and an edit above an entry moves its line.
rule line 26 · specs/extraction/entry-locations.sdp.md:26
The reader's Spec context carries the Spec's rows as its entry locations. Address resolution (recipe 25) adds the entry's value, file and line to each resolving row, and entry search (recipe 23) adds the line to each entry it matches.

7 unkeyed rules.

5. Recipes take parameters as data and ship as runnable files

spec:consumers.agent-surface.recipe-parameters

Recipes take parameters as data and ship as runnable files

spec:consumers.agent-surface.recipe-parametersUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 2 design entries · 2 pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A body reads its parameters by name, so a name it does not read would be dropped without a word, and a recipe with a sample would answer for the sample: a misspelled name would look like a successful call. A recipe therefore answers a name it does not take with that name and the names it does take, and nothing else. A body cannot import and the reader holds no recipe metadata, so each body declares its own names in its first statement, and the recipe check holds that declaration to the catalog.

Intent
problem
A recipe that takes its input in its own source makes a caller rewrite the body for each input, a long list included, and a script that runs a recipe must first cut its body out of the Markdown catalog.
outcome
Pass a recipe's parameter as data through the one evaluation sink, and ship every catalog body as a file a caller runs as written.
Behavior
rule line 19 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:19
sdp q takes --params with a JSON object, or --params @PATH with a file holding one, the path resolved from the working directory, and injects it as a fourth binding, params, beside g, graph and report. Without the flag params is an empty object. In these two forms, a value that is not valid JSON, JSON that is not an object (null, an array, a string, a number or a boolean), or a file that cannot be read is refused before the body runs, with exit 1, one line on stderr and no output on stdout.
rule line 20 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:20
--params is repeatable in three forms: a JSON object, @PATH naming a file that holds one, and KEY=@PATH binding the JSON value in the file, of any type, to params.KEY, with KEY on the lower-camel grammar. Objects merge at the top level from left to right, and a key given twice by any form is refused before the body runs, with exit 1, one line on stderr and no output on stdout, so a recipe takes a large file such as a base graph beside its other parameters.
rule line 21 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:21
The bindings g, graph and report keep their names and meaning beside params. The sink evaluates one operator-supplied body and adds no query vocabulary: a parameter is input to a body, never a verb.
rule line 22 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:22
Every recipe reads its parameters under the names the catalog states. A parameter with a documented sample falls back to it when absent, so each body runs as written; a required input with no sample, such as a base graph, a proposal or an imports file, returns diagnostics when absent. Recipe 4 reads its changed files from params.files.
rule.declaredNames line 23 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:23
Each catalog body opens by declaring the parameter names it takes, in the order the catalog's index lists them, and checks params against that list before it reads anything else; a recipe that takes no parameter declares an empty list.

no example exercises it

rule.unknownNames line 24 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:24
A recipe given a parameter name it does not take returns { unknownParams, accepts } as its whole answer, and sdp q exits 0; it never answers for its sample, for an empty input or for the names it does take in that case.

no example exercises it

rule.namesChecked line 25 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:25
The recipe check holds each body's declared names to the catalog's index and to the params names the body reads, and runs each body with a name it does not take.

no example exercises it

rule line 26 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:26
The package build writes each catalog body to dist/recipes/<NN>-<slug>.js, where NN is the two-digit recipe number and the slug is the recipe's heading in lower kebab case, and the package ships that directory. The catalog stays the one owner of the bodies; the files are derived, and the recipe test checks that each file equals its catalog body byte for byte.

5 unkeyed rules.

Design
acceptsPreamble line 30 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:30
const accepts = [...]; const unknownParams = Object.keys(params).filter((name) => !accepts.includes(name)); if (unknownParams.length > 0) return { unknownParams, accepts }; opens every catalog body as three statements on three lines, with the recipe's names in the brackets as double-quoted strings.

no citation recorded

unknownAnswer line 31 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.recipe-parameters.sdp.md:31
{ unknownParams, accepts } is the whole answer for a name a recipe does not take, where unknownParams lists every such name in the order params holds them, and accepts repeats the recipe's declared names.

no citation recorded

spec:consumers.agent-surface.design-recipes

Design work reads its answers from catalog recipes

spec:consumers.agent-surface.design-recipesUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/agent-surface.design-recipes.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
problem
Iterating on a design asks questions no recipe answers in one body: where a Pack's design stands, what a change to a Spec asks to follow, which decisions shape what, and which component dependencies cross a context or a layer. The first adopter answers each with its own script.
outcome
Answer each of those questions with a catalog recipe that runs as written, so design work reads them from the graph.
Behavior
rule line 19 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.design-recipes.sdp.md:19
The build backlog (recipe 1) gives each listed Spec its design columns, read from its Spec context.
rule line 20 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.design-recipes.sdp.md:20
Pack design (recipe 29) takes a Pack id in params.pack and returns the Pack context's design assembly as data, with members in authored order and the Pack's boundary. It returns a summary by default, full rows with detail: true, or mixed full and summary rows when detail lists member ids, in the shapes the answer-shapes Spec states. It returns found: false for an id that is no Pack.
rule line 21 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.design-recipes.sdp.md:21
Design-change impact (recipe 30) takes Spec ids in params.specs and returns every Spec that rests on them, transitively, through inbound refines, dependsOn, constrainedBy or decidedBy edges, each with the relation path that reaches it and its distance. For the changed Specs and every dependent it lists the units that satisfy it, the units that reference it, its enabled verifiers and its Packs. A references edge counts as a unit to notify and confers nothing.
rule line 22 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.design-recipes.sdp.md:22
Decision register (recipe 31) takes no parameter and returns one row per decision Spec, sorted by id: its title, stated rung, the decisions it supersedes and the decisions that supersede it, the decision-kind Specs it refines as refines and those that refine it as refinedBy, the reasons its relations state, the Specs that name it through decidedBy, its keyed open questions, and its Packs. It reads the graph alone; the ratified names stay in the decision registry document. Whether a refinement narrows a decision is that decision's own text or its relation's reason, never the field name.
rule line 23 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.design-recipes.sdp.md:23
Architecture crossings (recipe 32) takes no parameter and returns every uses edge whose two ends, each resolved to its own component directly or through memberOf, have components that both state a context and differ in it, or both state a layer and differ in it. Each row names both units, both components and what differs, and the totals tally the crossings by context pair and by layer pair, from -> to, so a corpus reads the direction of its dependencies at a glance. It reports and never refuses: a corpus gates its own architecture rule, as the architectural annotation decision leaves it. The totals also carry sameLayer and sameContext for resolved uses edges between distinct components that state the same layer or context, and bySameLayer per layer; edges within one component count in neither.
rule line 24 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.design-recipes.sdp.md:24
Each recipe body lives in the catalog and runs as written in the recipe test, and each reads its parameter as the recipe-parameters Spec states.

7. Example spaces report which values their examples cover

spec:consumers.agent-surface.example-space-coverage

Example spaces report which values their examples cover

spec:consumers.agent-surface.example-space-coverageUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

specs/consumers/agent-surface.example-space-coverage.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original design rendered a coverage heatmap from each example space: which combinations of its typed slots an example witnesses and which none does (docs/lineage/v0-design/04-authoring-surfaces.md §4 and §4.1, 06-extraction-and-validation.md §8). This Spec reports slot-value coverage; the glossary keeps witness for an example in an outcome class. Coverage is per slot value: no design pass has yet asked which combinations of slots no example exercises, and a combination grid grows with the product of the slots' sizes.

Intent
problem
The graph carries example spaces and bound points, but no reader value or recipe reports which literal slot values example children bind.
outcome
Report each literal slot value with the example children that bind it, and each value no child binds, before code exists.
Behavior
rule.decodedOnce line 22 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.example-space-coverage.sdp.md:22
The engine decodes each Spec's example space into its typed slots, and each example child's steps into its bound point, once, through the notation module that writes the space contracts, and the reader carries both on the Spec context; no recipe or projection parses slot notation a second time.

no example exercises it

rule.catalogRecipe line 23 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.example-space-coverage.sdp.md:23
Slot-value coverage is a catalog recipe, recipe 44, over the decoded reader values, listing each literal-union value with the example children that bind it and each value no child binds.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.example-space-coverage.uncovered-literal · enabled

rule.literalUnions line 24 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.example-space-coverage.sdp.md:24
The recipe enumerates slots typed as closed unions of quoted literals. It reports every other slot type, a boolean included, as not enumerable by this recipe, never as covered or as missing a value.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.example-space-coverage.number-not-enumerable · enabled, spec:consumers.agent-surface.example-space-coverage.uncovered-literal · enabled

8. The CLI names the engine that produced a result

spec:consumers.engine-provenance

The CLI names the engine that produced a result

spec:consumers.engine-provenanceUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 1 design entry · 1 pinned declaration · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/engine-provenance.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
problem
An adopter pinned to a build of the Protocol needs to name that build: the package version alone does not change between commits, so when a check changes with no Spec changed, nothing tells the engine moving from the corpus moving.
outcome
Let sdp --version name the package version and the commit the build came from, without putting either into the graph.
Behavior
rule line 22 · specs/consumers/engine-provenance.sdp.md:22
sdp --version prints one line, sdp <version> (<commit>), and exits 0. The version is the package's own version; the commit is the full hash the build was made from, or unknown when the build could not read one; a build from a checkout with uncommitted changes names the commit checked out when it ran.
rule line 23 · specs/consumers/engine-provenance.sdp.md:23
The build records the commit in a file beside the compiled CLI, and the CLI reads that file; it never runs git at run time.
rule line 24 · specs/consumers/engine-provenance.sdp.md:24
The build reads the commit from git first. When git gives no full commit, it reads the archive's substituted commit file; a full commit there names the archived revision, and an absent, unsubstituted or malformed file leaves the commit unknown.
rule line 25 · specs/consumers/engine-provenance.sdp.md:25
Neither the version nor the commit enters the graph, a projection or a generated contract, so a derived artifact stays a function of the corpus alone.

4 unkeyed rules.

Design
archiveCommit line 28 · specs/consumers/engine-provenance.sdp.md:28
.git-archive-commit contains $Format:%H$ in a checkout and is marked export-subst in .gitattributes, so git archives carry their full commit. The build reads the trimmed file only as a full Git object name, never as a command or an abbreviated hash.

9. Validation re-runs while an author edits carriers

spec:consumers.validate-watch

Validation re-runs while an author edits carriers

spec:consumers.validate-watchUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:adopter-speed-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/validate-watch.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
problem
An author editing a Spec re-runs sdp validate by hand after every save.
outcome
Let sdp validate --watch re-run the one validation path on every carrier change and stay alive after findings, as a loop for authoring and never a second validation path.
Behavior
rule line 19 · specs/consumers/validate-watch.sdp.md:19
sdp validate --watch [root] installs its watcher first, then runs the same validate path sdp validate runs, from scratch, once at start and again after every carrier create, change, delete or rename under the root.
rule line 20 · specs/consumers/validate-watch.sdp.md:20
A carrier ends in .sdp.md, .sdp.gherkin or .sdp.ts. The watcher ignores the directories discovery skips, the configured exclusion prefixes and every non-carrier path other than the rules files and parameter files --rules names, which it watches wherever they live, as spec:validation.corpus-rules#rule.watchReruns and spec:validation.corpus-rules#rule.watchedParams state; a removed watched directory and an event with no filename each schedule a run because their affected carriers cannot be named.
rule line 21 · specs/consumers/validate-watch.sdp.md:21
Events that arrive while a run is in progress coalesce into one pending run.
rule.operatorStop line 22 · specs/consumers/validate-watch.sdp.md:22
Findings print as sdp validate prints them and the process stays alive; operator SIGINT terminates the process with exit 0 even while a rules body is active, without waiting for it. No further rules file runs or output is written after the stop.

no example exercises it

rule line 23 · specs/consumers/validate-watch.sdp.md:23
For sdp validate, --watch cannot combine with --check-clean, and it re-runs on carrier edits and on edits to the files --rules names, and never on source edits, so an author re-runs validation after editing an anchor. This rule restricts no other verb's --watch, which its own Spec states.

4 unkeyed rules.

specs/model/design-maturity.sdp.md

1 open question and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design's designed stage meant a Spec's key concepts were settled before code (docs/lineage/v0-design/01-core-primitives.md §1.4 and §8). The Protocol's readiness describes the maturity of intent. The graph therefore derives what design a Spec carries beside readiness, without adding a rung, floor clause or delivery fact. A new rung would change the locked readiness values, a floor clause reading Design would close that section's shape, and a design fact would mix design with realization signals.

Intent
problem
A reviewer or an implementer cannot tell from readiness alone which Specs carry a settled design and which carry only intent, and the first adopter's owner asked for Specs whose key concepts are designed as stubs before code.
outcome
Show what design a Spec carries in values the graph derives, so the backlog and a review can tell a designed Spec from one that states only its intent.
assumptions
  • The design columns tell a Spec with pinned declarations and keyed entries from one that states only its intent.

11. Components are designed ahead of their code

spec:model.planned-architecture

Components are designed ahead of their code

spec:model.planned-architectureDomain Model · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:corpus-checks-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 6 design entries · 1 pinned declaration · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/model/planned-architecture.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design declared a component before its code, as a Component node with a layer, a bounded context and a capability, kept in an architecture folder and reconciled with its code anchors and the Specs (docs/lineage/v0-design/03-graph-metamodel.md §2.5; 04-authoring-surfaces.md §7). Its runtime chapter separated what a unit requires from the provider that supplies it, the provider a composition root selects and the one a test puts in its place, and gave one mechanism the ownership of runtime composition (05-runtime-anchors.md §1, §3.3, §7).

The Protocol records the architecture the code realizes. A component: anchor states its layer and context, and anchored memberOf and uses edges join the code units. Under the architectural annotation decision, a component no code realizes is a Spec, and the graph holds no node for it until an anchor exists. The first adopter states its component list and its context rule in prose (libar-platform/design/PLAN.md §2.1) and checks context isolation over anchored uses in its own script (libar-platform/design/tools/check.py). The owner ruled that the architectural annotation decision stands: a component designed before its code is a component design Spec, and the component: anchor that later realizes it satisfies that Spec, which is the join a comparison reads.

Choosing a provider stays prose. The original's distinctions between the interface a unit requires, the providers that supply it, the one a composition root selects and the one a test substitutes help a reader, and none of them needs graph structure beyond uses to be compared. Keeping one composition mechanism per application is a corpus's own architecture rule when the corpus wants it, stated in a constraint Spec and checked by its own corpus rule. A component design names its component with the keys a component anchor uses, so the comparison reads the same words on both sides, and a key the design leaves out is not compared, so a design states only what it has decided; a design that has decided its component uses nothing says none, which a left-out key cannot say.

Intent
problem
A design ahead of its code cannot state the components it adds, their layer and context and what they use, in a form the graph compares with the components the code later anchors.
outcome
Let a design name the components it will add, with their layer, context and uses, and compare that design with the anchored components once code exists.
risks
  • A planned component kept apart from its realization is a second place for the component to drift, which is why the architectural annotation decision refused a separate architecture file and why the design lives in a Spec the realizing anchor satisfies.
Behavior

0 unkeyed rules.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.architectural-annotation

    Architectural significance is annotated on the anchor of the unit that realizes it. A code anchor may carry role, the architectural pattern the unit plays; a component: anchor may additionally carry layer, one of edge, application, domain, adapter, or infrastructure, and context, its bounded context. The component: anchor is anchored architecture: it is the declared component, and there is no separate architecture file, because the anchor sits where the component is realized. It is not the original design's declared Component that could exist before code; an unrealized component lives in Specs and never as an invented CodeNode. A role is a free, corpus-owned vocabulary whose taxonomy the census renders with counts from the graph; service, decider, projection, read-model, codec, contract, barrel, and utility are the lineage set, not a closed list. layer is a closed set, and a value outside it is an envelope error; layer or context on a non-component anchor is an envelope error. All three attributes are optional, and omission is lawful.

12. An open question may name who decides it, its links, a provisional reading and a re-entry trigger

spec:model.open-question-fields

An open question may name who decides it, its links, a provisional reading and a re-entry trigger

spec:model.open-question-fieldsBusiness Rule · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 7 design entries · 1 pinned declaration · 2 decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original design gave an open question an owner and a list of links to decision records, discussions and tickets, beside its text and its blocking flag (docs/lineage/v0-design/01-core-primitives.md §2.1). A question key gives a question an address and nothing more, so the first adopter keeps the rest beside the graph. Its decision register (libar-platform/design/decisions/register.json, described in design/advisors/register.md) records for each open decision its sources, who decides it as a class (tactical, delegated or owner) and an advisor lens, the provisional reading the design proceeds on, and a lean. It also records a status, the work unit it blocks, dates and who checked the lean. This Spec captures the part that states something about the question and leaves the work record outside.

A TypeScript open-question list that cannot be read statically drops whole, blocking questions included. A failure under one of the four fields is an error, because the fields arrived with no carrier relying on a lossy reading; a failure in a question's text, its blocking flag or the list itself keeps the warning every other non-static TypeScript section property gives.

Intent
problem
A question's text and blocking flag do not say who settles it, what it rests on, or what the design assumes until it is settled, so an adopter keeps a register beside the graph that repeats each question.
outcome
Let an open question carry who decides it, the sources it rests on, the reading the design proceeds on and, on a deferral, what brings it back, without a status.
risks
  • A field for who decides invites fields for when and for what state the question is in, which would rebuild a workflow tracker inside the Spec.
Rule

The world writes one TypeScript carrier for a story-altitude rule Spec stating idea, with a title, an Intent outcome, one rule and an open-question list holding one blocking question. Every value is static apart from the construct the point names: a question text or blocking flag written as a function call, or a spread of another list beside the question.

rule line 29 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:29
An open question may carry four optional fields beside its text, flag and key, namely who decides it, the links it rests on, its provisional reading and its re-entry trigger; a question without them stays lawful.
rule line 30 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:30
Who decides a question names the person, role or body whose ruling settles it. It authorizes nothing, gates no edit, and no validator compares it with the author of a change.
rule line 31 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:31
Who decides a question is one lowercase kebab token the corpus owns, on the grammar a role uses, such as owner or delegated. The graph holds no person or role to point at, so the value references nothing, and the Protocol ships no list of values.
rule line 32 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:32
In the Markdown carrier the four fields ride labelled sub-items indented under the question's own line, decider:, links:, provisional: and trigger:, each at most once and each one line, so the question line stays as authored. They are the only indented field lines the body grammar admits, and the TypeScript carrier carries the same four fields on the question object.
rule.fieldFailureError line 33 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:33
In the TypeScript carrier, a value under any of the four fields that cannot be read statically is an extraction error at that field, and the Spec's whole open-question list drops with it.

rule.droppedListWarning line 34 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:34
In the TypeScript carrier, a question text or blocking flag that cannot be read statically, or a spread in the list, drops the Spec's whole open-question list, blocking questions included, with the lossy warning extract/non-static-section; only a failure under the four fields is an error.

spec:model.open-question-fields.dropped-list-warns · enabled

rule line 35 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:35
A link is a Spec id or an entry address the question rests on, and nothing else. Each is checked as a mention is: a missing target or entry is an error, and a target with no declared relation either way raises the conformance/prose-mentions warning for that pair. A link mints no relation, and a document outside the graph is named in the question's text as prose, because the graph holds no identity for it to resolve.
rule line 36 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:36
The provisional reading is one line stating what the design assumes while the question is open. It is intent, never a ruling.
rule line 37 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:37
A question carries at most one provisional line. A worked proposal for settling it is a decision Spec whose Decision section holds its decision, context, rationales, alternatives and consequences, stated at the rung its record earns. Each shaped Spec names it through decidedBy, so a decision below defined holds that Spec below ready under the typed-dependency floor.
rule line 38 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:38
A re-entry trigger is one line naming what brings a deferred Spec back, such as a named reader the shipped views do not serve. It sits on the blocking question that holds the deferral, and the open-question register reports questions that carry one apart from design holds, so no reader tells the two apart by their wording.
rule line 39 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:39
An open question carries no status, date, blocked work unit or record of who checked it. A settled question leaves the Spec, a ruling that passes the ADR three-part test lands as a decision Spec the shaped Specs name through decidedBy, and the rest of the history stays in git and in the adopter's own records.
rule line 40 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:40
Whether a question holds the readiness floor stays its [blocking] flag alone; none of the four fields moves a floor.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.adopt-the-nouns

    The Protocol adopts established delivery nouns and rejects process state-machine and lifecycle gating.

  • spec:decisions.planning-truths-placement

    Each planning-truth type lives in its ruled home. Work-item dependency truth rides dependsOn edges, with independence as absence of the edge and scheduling phrases never authored. Decision gates live on decision-kind Specs, linked by decidedBy. Do-not-reopen rows split by what they carry: a tradeoff refusal becomes a decision-kind Spec, which a later decision that supersedes it replaces whole and a later decision that refines it narrows for one case, either under the ADR three-part test; a row that restates a behavior guarantee already homed on a carrying Spec stays on that Spec and changes by ordinary Spec revision; a hold stays a blocking open question on its own Spec and is never minted as a decision. A lawful non-decision stays in the plan record as evidence. A deferral carries its re-entry trigger in the trigger field of its own blocking open question, and declares dependsOn separately when a true precondition exists. Exclusive ownership is one Spec identity per deliverable with consumers depending on it. Selection-pressure heuristics are advisory only, carried as behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec or in recipes. Session law splits separately, across behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec, the delivery-session on-ramp's handoff rule, and the plan file. The briefs index shape is retired as a carrier of law.

13. A rule or flow entry may carry a key that addresses it

spec:model.rule-keys

A rule or flow entry may carry a key that addresses it

spec:model.rule-keysBusiness Rule · storyready floor ready

specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design gave a behavior rule an optional id, so the rule could later be promoted to a Spec of its own, and an optional rationale (docs/lineage/v0-design/01-core-primitives.md §2.2). The Protocol kept promotion and dropped the id. An unkeyed rule has no address, so a review finding, a register row or an example cannot name it; a key gives it an address. Open questions carry optional keys on the entry-address key grammar; this Spec follows that pattern for rules.

Intent
problem
An inline rule has no identity but its position and its text, so anything outside the Spec that cites one rule breaks silently when the rules above it move or the rule is reworded.
outcome
Let an author key a rule or flow entry, so a review, a register row or an example can name the entry it is about.
Rule
rule line 27 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:27
Every entry of a Spec's primary behavior owner may carry an optional key on the open-question key grammar: the rule: and flow: entries of Behavior, the entries of Rule and Contract, and the entries and rule: entries of Workflow. One Spec keeps one key namespace across them, unique among its keyed entries, and an unkeyed entry stays lawful and has no address.
rule line 28 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:28
A key sits in a marker at the start of the entry's text, after the rule: or flow: label where the entry has one, as in - rule: [#graphOnly] The Studio is a projection. and - [#oneFamily] Every validator belongs to one family., the shape an open question's marker uses, so one form serves labelled and plain entries.
rule line 29 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:29
Every keyed entry is addressed as spec:<id>#rule.<key> whatever its section, because a Spec uses one primary behavior owner. The address resolves while the Spec carries an entry with that key and fails validation in every Spec that names it once the key is renamed or removed.
rule line 30 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:30
A rule address is refused in every id slot, as every entry address is, so no anchor targets a rule and no delivery fact attaches to one.
rule line 31 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:31
An example names the keyed rules it exercises on its verifies relation: the target is an object with target and exercises, a list of the verified Spec's rule keys, beside an optional reason. A key the verified Spec does not carry is a conformance error at the relation, as a missing entry address is. The list mints no edge and confers no delivery fact, so verifies stays whole-Spec, and a rule-coverage recipe reads it to report which keyed rules a bound example exercises and which none does.
rule line 32 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:32
A keyed entry carries its key and its text and nothing else; why a rule holds is the Spec's narrative, or a decision Spec named through decidedBy when the why passes the ADR three-part test.
rule line 33 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:33
A keyed rule promoted to a Spec of its own leaves its address behind, because promotion moves the content out, and every mention of that address fails until it names the new Spec.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.checked-mentions

    A Spec id in narrative or section text, outside gwt and gwt-vocabulary fences, is a mention. A mention that does not resolve is a conformance error. A mention of another Spec that shares no declared relation with the mentioning Spec, in either direction, is one warning per mentioning Spec and target Spec pair, whatever the number of locations; an address on the mentioning Spec's own id is checked for its entry and never warned. An entry address is a Spec id followed by #, the section name design, ui, question, rule, or term, a dot, and the entry's lower-camel ASCII key, as in spec:<id>#design.<key> or spec:<id>#question.<key>. A design or ui address resolves when the Spec exists and that section holds the key as its own key, other than description; a question address resolves when the Spec exists and one of its open questions carries that key; a term address resolves when the Spec exists and one of its Model terms carries that key. The # sub-part is reserved for the entry address in every namespace: a Spec's own id, a relation target, a Pack member or model reference, an anchor id or target, and the specId and ref builders all refuse it. A mention mints no edge, and the reader gains no join.

  • spec:decisions.shipped-projections-frozen

    Re-specifying the shipped Design Review, census, Mermaid, or Gherkin projection is refused. These four projections are the ruled read surfaces over the one graph. A later decision Spec that supersedes this one replaces the ruling whole; a decision Spec that refines this one narrows it for one projection or one rendering and leaves the rest frozen. Either passes the ADR three-part test.

14. An authored relation may carry its reason

spec:model.relation-reasons

An authored relation may carry its reason

spec:model.relation-reasonsBusiness Rule · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 5 design entries · no pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design let a relation say why it holds: a rationale on refines, a strength on dependsOn, an aspect on constrainedBy and a reason on supersedes (docs/lineage/v0-design/01-core-primitives.md §4; 04-authoring-surfaces.md §1.3). The Protocol's relations carry a type, a target and a claim; a relation without a reason leaves the explanation of why a Spec rests on another in narrative prose a reader has to find. The prose-ownership decision gives free prose a typed owner; this Spec gives a relation's reason its home on that relation.

The first adopter meets the reverse case. When its mention audit reported Spec pairs named in prose with no relation behind them, it declared the relations that were missing dependencies and kept the rest as prose, each listed with a one-line reason no typed relation fits (libar-platform/docs/feedback/sdp-feedback-01.md, "The mention warnings were mostly missing edges"; libar-platform/design/tools/prose-mentions.json). A reason on a relation says why an edge holds; a listed mention reason says why none does.

Intent
problem
A reviewer reading a relation cannot see why it holds, and a reviewer reading a mention left as prose cannot tell an intended pointer from a forgotten dependency without a list kept outside the graph.
outcome
Let an author say in one line why a Spec refines, depends on, is constrained by, is decided by or supersedes another, beside the relation itself.
Rule
rule line 23 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:23
An authored relation may carry one optional reason, a single line of prose owned by that relation from that Spec to that target.
rule line 24 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:24
One optional reason serves every relation type. No strength, aspect or other attribute rides a relation, except the rule keys an example's verifies lists, which the rule-coverage recipe reads.
rule line 25 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:25
A reason is intent, as its relation is; it confers no delivery fact, moves no readiness floor and changes nothing its edge confers, and a relation without one stays lawful.
rule line 26 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:26
In the envelope a relation target is a plain Spec id or an object with target and optional reason; a declared verifies object may also carry exercises. A target-only object reads as the plain id, plain ids and objects may mix in one relation, and no target is written twice. The TypeScript carrier passes the same reason beside the target.
rule line 27 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:27
A reason on supersedes says what the newer decision replaces, and a reason on a refines from one decision to another says which part of the older decision the newer one narrows.
rule line 28 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:28
A reason reaches readers with its relation through the graph, so a projection or a recipe reads it from the edge and never from the carrier.
rule line 29 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:29
A mention left as prose carries no reason in the Spec. A corpus may keep the mentions it intends as rows of from, to and reason beside its Specs and pass them to the mention audit as a parameter; the audit reports the pairs a row matches apart from the rest, each with its reason, and lists the rows that match no current pair, while the validator reads no such list and its warning stands.

7 unkeyed rules.

Design
envelopeTarget line 33 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:33
a relation target is a Spec id or { target: <spec id>, reason: <one line> }, the two mixing in one list and a single target taking either form; a declared verifies object may also carry exercises, and an object with another key, an empty reason, or a reason on two lines is refused; an object carrying only target reads as the plain id.
builderArgument line 34 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:34
each TypeScript relation builder takes an optional second argument, dependsOn(target, { reason }), with verifies(target, { reason, exercises }) also taking the rule keys, and a builder called without it writes a plain declared relation.
edgeReason line 35 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:35
an authored graph edge carries an optional reason, and the reader's relation ends carry it; the guarantees recipe (3), dependency footing (21), the planning slice (19) and the decision register (31) show it beside the relation.
gherkinRelations line 36 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:36
no Gherkin form is invented for a relation reason, because relation tags carry no prose; a Spec that needs one is authored in Markdown or TypeScript.
intendedMentions line 37 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:37
the mention audit (recipe 22) takes params.intended, rows { from, to, reason } keyed by Spec ids, and returns intended, the unbacked pairs a row matches with its reason, kept apart from the remaining pairs, and staleIntended, the rows that match no current pair.

15. A Pack is read from a named perspective

spec:consumers.review-perspectives

A Pack is read from a named perspective

spec:consumers.review-perspectivesUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 4 design entries · 1 pinned declaration · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design gave every reader one reading surface, each reading from their own concern: the analyst, the domain engineer, the architect, the tester, the designer and the agent (docs/lineage/v0-design/04-authoring-surfaces.md §6). The first adopter iterates each capability's design through advisor lenses, its runtime platform, the domain, operations and the product, each a written list of the questions its field asks, run over the same Pack by the same pass brief (libar-platform/design/advisors/lenses/, libar-platform/design/advisors/task-pass.md). It asks for a lens to be a filter over the same capability that reorders and emphasizes questions, entries, examples and constraints and opens the same Specs, with no new Spec kind and no compulsory sequence of stages (libar-platform/docs/feedback/sdp-feedback-02.md, item 28). The Protocol takes the member filter and the order and leaves each member's content whole; emphasis inside a member stays the reader's.

The owner ruled the word: perspective. The Spec Studio keeps lens for its graph views, its Packs, capabilities, architecture, tests and evidence views, and discipline stays the filter by kind or section. The adopter's advisor lens is a reader's concern, not a view of the graph, so in the Protocol's terms it is a perspective.

Intent
actor
A reviewer or an agent who reads a Pack for one concern, such as the domain model, operations or the runtime platform.
problem
Every reading of a Pack shows every member in the same order with the same emphasis, so a reader with one concern sorts it by hand, and an adopter keeps its perspectives as prose briefs the graph cannot apply.
outcome
Let a reviewer read the same Pack from one perspective at a time, filtered and ordered for that perspective, without a new kind or a stage.
Behavior
rule.contentIntact line 22 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:22
A perspective filters and orders a Pack's members and leaves each selected member's content intact; every row opens the same Spec, and the whole Pack stays one step away.

no example exercises it

rule line 23 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:23
A perspective adds no kind, readiness, stage or sequence; reading a Pack from one perspective records nothing, and no perspective is required before another or before ready is stated.
rule line 24 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:24
The corpus owns its perspectives and their questions; the Protocol supplies the filter and ships no list of perspectives.
rule line 25 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:25
A perspective is corpus data: a JSON object the corpus keeps beside its briefs and passes to the perspective filter, a catalog recipe, through --params. The reader loads no perspective file, and no validator lists or checks perspectives, so no registry forms.
rule line 26 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:26
A perspective selects members by Spec id or id prefix, kind, section presence, Design key with an optional value, question key, and authored relation type with a stated direction; it selects component layer or context only through the member's code unit bindings, satisfying or referencing, that the perspective names; it infers nothing from prose, paths or imports.
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:27
A member selected by a Design key, including the layer and context keys a component design states, is selected on declared intent; a member selected through a binding's component is selected on anchored structure; each row names which, and the two are never merged into one architecture answer.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:28
Values within one selector are alternatives and different selectors combine as requirements; an unsupported selector is a diagnostic in the result, and a valid selector that matches nothing is an explicit empty result.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:29
Members keep the manifest's authored order unless the perspective gives an explicit priority order, authored order breaking ties; every selected member's blocking questions stay visible whatever else the perspective filters out.

7 unkeyed rules.

Design
perspectiveObject line 33 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:33
{ "name": "models", "select": { "kinds": ["model"] } } selects the members of kind model. A perspective is { name, select, order } with select and order optional, and its selectors are ids, idPrefixes, kinds, sections, designKeys, questionKeys, relations and bindings, each optional; different selectors combine as requirements. An absent selector imposes no requirement, a present empty list matches no member, and an absent or empty select object selects every member. A designKeys item is { key, value } with value optional; a relations item is { type, direction, target } with direction out or in and target optional; bindings is { via, layers, contexts }, where via is required and lists satisfies or references, and absent layers or contexts impose no restriction. order lists Spec ids by priority, authored order breaking ties.

no citation recorded

perspectiveRecipe line 34 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:34
recipe 37, the perspective filter, takes params.pack and params.perspective and returns { pack, perspective, totals: { members, selected }, diagnostics, selected, notSelected }.
perspectiveRows line 35 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:35
each selected row is { id, matchedOn: [{ selector, value, claim }], blockingQuestions: [{ address, question }] } in the perspective's order and then authored order; claim is declared for a match on authored intent and anchored for a match through a binding; notSelected lists the remaining member ids in authored order.
perspectiveDiagnostics line 36 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:36
an unknown selector, a value of the wrong type or a bindings selector with no via is a diagnostic row { selector, problem }, and the recipe still applies the selectors it understood.

16. A context bundle is composed per invocation within a stated budget

spec:consumers.context-bundle

A context bundle is composed per invocation within a stated budget

spec:consumers.context-bundleUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:adopter-speed-v1, pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 17 design entries · 7 pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original design precomputed graph slices for different reading scopes and a prompt bundle for one Spec. The Protocol keeps context bundle for the reading material of one design pass, composed on demand.

The first adopter's design passes assemble the same reading material by hand: the Pack design, member questions, dependency footing, pinned declarations and carrying Spec text where the graph answer falls short. Its perspectives read the same Pack for different concerns. The agent front door composes a bundle on each invocation; the bundle is never a committed answer in the graph's name. It builds on Pack design.

At an adopter's scale a bundle is mostly structure, so its shape is compact. Each member and each example row names its carrier file once. A cut entry without an entry address keeps only its line, since its row and its place in the bundle already name it. A question, a pinned value or a member example's steps appears in one place. Pinned declarations stay whole by default, because a builder and a test author hold to them. A caller whose scope still does not fit may let the bundle cut them to their entry addresses, and then reads each one in its Spec when the pass needs it. A partial bundle stays refused, because a bundle missing members would read as the whole scope.

A scope can hold more design than one budget allows after every cut, as the first adopter's largest Packs do. A caller then reads the bundle in parts: the same bundle, split between members into ordered parts that each fit the budget, whose members together are the whole scope. In parts a cut is taken only when an item, a member or the boundary, does not fit a part by itself, so a part keeps the design a single bundle would have cut. A repeated header that exceeds the budget alone is named as one oversized item; otherwise each item that exceeds the budget alone is named. No part is returned in either case.

Intent
actor
An agent starting one design pass over a Pack or an ordered list of Specs.
problem
Each pass assembles the same reading material by running the same recipes and joining their answers by hand, and nothing bounds what it hands the model.
outcome
Give an agent the reading material for one design pass in one composed slice of the graph within a stated budget, so no session hand-assembles it.
Behavior
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:27
A bundle is a catalog recipe that takes its scope and its budget as recipe parameters; it adds no entrance and no query verb.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:28
A bundle is composed from the graph on each invocation by the reader every recipe uses; nothing is precomputed, saved or committed, and two invocations over the same graph with the same parameters compose the same bundle.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:29
A bundle takes one scope: pack, a Pack id, or specs, an ordered list of Spec ids. For specs the members are the listed Specs in the given order and the boundary is each member's one-hop neighbors through the four typed relations both ways, with verifies and supersedes apart, as the Pack boundary is built. Both scopes or neither is a diagnostic result. A changeset fills specs from the impacted Spec ids changed-file impact reports, and a Pack's open questions are read from the Pack bundle, not from a third scope.
rule line 30 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:30
With pack, a bundle may take members, an ordered subset of the Pack's member ids, which the perspective filter returns; it keeps the Pack's framing and boundary, lists only those members in that order, and states that it is a subset, so one filter implementation serves both recipes.
rule line 31 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:31
A bundle for a Pack carries the Pack design assembly, its members in authored order with their design columns and its boundary, then each member's open questions with their addresses and lines, its dependency footing, its pinned declarations and its examples.
rule line 32 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:32
The budget is a hard limit on a successful bundle, counted in UTF-16 code units, the length a recipe body reads, of the compact JSON.stringify of the value the recipe returns, its scope, budget and left-out statement included; sdp q --json prints a longer indented form, and the budget never measures printed text. The bundle also reports a token estimate labeled as an estimate, so no model's tokenizer binds the Protocol.
rule.oneCopy line 33 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:33
A bundle carries a member's open questions only in its questions, a pinned declaration's value only in its member's Design section, and an example's steps only in its own member row when the example is a member of the bundle; an example outside the bundle keeps its steps in the row of each member it refines or verifies.

no example exercises it

rule.cutOrder line 34 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:34
When the scope exceeds the budget, the bundle cuts in a fixed order and stops at the first cut after which it fits: boundary rows down to their ids, footing rows down to their ids, member narrative, example step text, non-blocking question text, remaining section values other than pinned declarations, then, only when the caller allows it, pinned declarations down to their entry addresses. It never cuts member ids, the stated rung, the floor reached, the stated next rung, blocking questions or entry addresses, and it cuts nothing else.

no example exercises it

rule.declarationAddresses line 35 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:35
A caller allows the last cut by passing declarations: "addresses"; without it, or with declarations: "whole", pinned declarations stay whole, and any other value is a diagnostic result.

no example exercises it

rule line 36 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:36
Without part, when the protected content alone exceeds the budget after every permitted cut, the recipe returns a budget-exceeded result as data and no partial bundle: the requested scope, the budget, and the minimum count the protected content needs in the same unit; sdp q exits 0, because the result is the body's return and not a refusal.
rule line 37 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:37
A bundle gives the file and line of an entry or a binding in place of a source excerpt, because the reader never reads source.
rule line 38 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:38
A bundle states its scope, its budget and what it left out to stay within the budget, so a reader knows what to read in the Specs themselves.
rule line 39 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:39
A bundle carries facts from the graph and no instructions of its own; the brief that tells an agent what to look for stays the corpus's own text.
rule.parts line 40 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:40
With part, the 1-based index of the part to return, a bundle comes in ordered parts, each within the budget, and the members of its parts, read in part order, are the bundle's members in order, each once.

rule.partBoundaries line 41 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:41
A part boundary falls between items and never inside one: the boundary is the first item and each member is one item, in the scope's order, and each part holds the longest run of items after the part before it that fits the budget.

rule.partCuts line 42 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:42
In parts the bundle tries the cut order one cut at a time, starting from no cut, splits the scope at each stage and takes the first stage at which every part fits the budget, each part measured whole in the shape it returns: its repeated fields, its leftOut, the boundary in part 1 and the final part.of; every part takes that stage's cuts and lists them in leftOut.

Every part repeats the scope, the budget, the declaration mode, the cuts taken, its own place among the parts and, for a Pack scope, the Pack's id, title and framing, so each part reads on its own; only the first part carries the boundary.

rule.sameParts line 44 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:44

rule.oversizedItem line 45 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:45
